text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The two coalition party leaders intentionally put off ratification of decrees presented by the other alliance wing.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright highlights the importance the United States gives to the continuation of secularism in Turkey.
- A private bodyguard force of the ruling Islamist party wears similar uniforms to that of militants from the Hamas and Hizbollah organisations.
- Turkey is to sign a contract to purchase 34 helicopters from France.
- Suspicion grows that the state made use of 73 jailed Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels in mystery murders.
- Bread prices in Istanbul are to go up to 20,000 Turkish Lira for a 225 gram loaf by March 1.
- The level of vehicle production decreased by 23 percent in January from a year earlier.
- Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit rejects the possibility of his party merging with another leftist party.
